Magazine · 2026

Revue Lumière, a redesign

A cultural monthly that had grown loud, set again on nine columns and two typefaces - so that long reads run wide and short ones sit quietly in the margin.

Client
Revue Lumière
Role
Art direction, typography
Year
2026
Format
Monthly, 148 pages

The brief

Revue Lumière had grown loud: six typefaces, a cover line on every inch and a new section every season. The editors wanted readers to stay longer with each piece - without losing the newsstand.

My part

I led two designers and the photo desk for nine months. We cut the magazine to two faces and one cover image, drew a nine-column grid and wrote the style sheet the editors now use without us.

The result

Newsstand sales rose for the first time in a decade, and the time readers spend with an issue doubled in the reader survey. The letters page asked us to never change it again.
